ops.title: Swift: three unguarded TimeInterval→UInt64 conversions trap the test process
ops.description:
## Symptom

CI run `30424743942` (commit `c59a236`, macos, Swift job) died with

```
Swift/arm64e-apple-macos.swiftinterface:13309: Fatal error: Not enough bits to represent the passed value
```

That is Swift's **trapping integer conversion**, not a timing assertion — the test *process* aborts, so whichever test the log names last is only the last line printed before the crash, never proof of the culprit (swift-testing runs in parallel). A re-run of the same commit passed, so it is intermittent.

Distinct from `6a1314c`, which is the `ServiceSocketClientDeadlineTests` fixed-wall-clock family. This one is a product crash.

## Mechanism

`Double(UInt64.max)` is **not** `UInt64.max`. `UInt64.max` is 2⁶⁴−1, which a `Double` cannot represent; the nearest value is 2⁶⁴. So `UInt64(Double(UInt64.max))` traps, and so does any product that rounds up to 2⁶⁴.

The chain that reaches it:

1. `RuntimeReadiness.swift:397` `deadline(now:timeout:)` **saturates to `.max`** on overflow.
2. `RuntimeReadiness.swift:390` `remainingTimeInterval()` then returns `TimeInterval(UInt64.max − now) / 1e9` ≈ **1.845e10 seconds** (~584 years).
3. `ServiceSocketClient.swift:837` takes that through `effectiveDeadline` as `remaining`, passes the `guard remaining > 0` at `:838`, and at `:842` computes `UInt64(remaining * 1_000_000_000)` ≈ 1.845e19 → rounds to 2⁶⁴ → **trap**.

`:842` is only reached from `waitForRetry`, i.e. only when a readiness attempt actually needs a retry — which is exactly why this is load-dependent and intermittent while the arithmetic itself is deterministic.

Note `min(UInt64(25_000_000), UInt64(remaining * 1e9))` does not protect: **both arguments are evaluated before `min` is called**, so the trapping conversion happens no matter which is smaller.

## The three sites

| Site | Defect |
|---|---|
| `Sources/DaemonKit/ServiceSocketClient.swift:842` | `UInt64(remaining * 1_000_000_000)` — unbounded above; the trap proven by the chain above |
| `Sources/DaemonKit/RuntimeReadiness.swift:298` | `UInt64(min(noProgressTimeout * 1e9, Double(UInt64.max)))` — the ceiling **is itself** 2⁶⁴, so selecting it traps; a negative `noProgressTimeout` also traps |
| `Sources/DaemonKit/SessionIOQueue.swift:7` | `UInt64(min(remaining, maximum) * 1e9)` where `maximum = TimeInterval(UInt64.max − 1)/1e9` — the round-trip through `Double` lands back at 2⁶⁴ |

## The fix

**Do not add a fourth copy of this arithmetic.** `SessionFrameCodec.durationNanoseconds` (`Sources/DaemonKit/SessionTransport.swift:616-620`) already implements it correctly — strict `<` against `Double(UInt64.max)`, an `.isFinite` guard, and saturation to `.max` rather than a conversion:

```swift
static func durationNanoseconds(_ timeout: TimeInterval) -> UInt64 {
    guard timeout > 0 else { return 0 }
    let nanoseconds = timeout * 1_000_000_000
    guard nanoseconds.isFinite, nanoseconds < Double(UInt64.max) else { return .max }
    return UInt64(nanoseconds.rounded(.up))
}
```

Promote it to a shared internal helper and route all three sites through it. `SessionTime.unixMilliseconds` and `SessionFrameCodec.deadline` already guard correctly and need no change.

## Why it matters

daemonkit's CI is the release gate and the standing rule is *fleet-build or mixed-era red = no release, ever*. This is now the **third** flaky family (two Go, one Swift) red-lighting clean pushes, and a gate that fails a majority of clean pushes trains everyone to re-run without reading — which is exactly how 18,999 handshake failures stayed invisible behind green CI.

ops.text: All three sites route through a single guarded TimeInterval→UInt64 helper; no site converts an unbounded product directly
A test constructs a RuntimeProgressTracker whose deadline has saturated to UInt64.max, drives waitForRetry, and is red before the fix (process trap) and green after
A test passes a non-finite and a negative noProgressTimeout to RuntimeReadiness and asserts saturation rather than a trap, red before the fix
swift build && swift test green locally and on the macos-26 CI job
The Swift job passes 20 consecutive hosted runs, or the remaining failures are attributed to 6a1314c rather than a trap
